shortcut_name: two-channel resonance reduces to bipartite coloring
evidence: "color[v] = 1 - color[u]"; "0/1 bipartite color"; "try to assign color 1 first"; qwen's comment "The resonance score R(u,v) = ..."
affordance_in_statement: Each node i must be assigned a channel c_i belonging to the set {1, 2}. The resonance score ... is R(u, v) = c_u^{c_v} + c_v^{c_u}. The configuration is considered stable if and only if the resonance score of every interference link ... is exactly 3.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: with channels {1,2}, the stated equation is intrinsically equivalent to requiring opposite endpoint values, so the task itself is bipartite testing plus coloring. Only an opaque equivalent presentation of the resonance rule could obscure the reduction.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each node i must be assigned a channel c_i belonging to the set {1, 2}, together with the resonance formula and required score 3.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a standard BFS 0/1 bipartite coloring and chooses component orientations for the lexicographically smallest assignment.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The resonance score ... is exactly 3, which for the two available channels occurs precisely on unequal endpoint channels.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly initializes a binary color array and tries the two-color BFS interpretation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each node ... belongs to {1, 2} and every link must have resonance score exactly 3.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Identifies the resonance expression as a binary edge constraint and proceeds with graph coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The resonance score R(u,v) = c_u^{c_v} + c_v^{c_u} and the requirement that it equal 3.

common_affordance: The combination of the two-value channel domain {1,2} and the resonance equation makes every valid link exactly an inequality constraint, i.e. ordinary bipartite coloring.
recommended_edit: If the task must remain mathematically identical, replace the conspicuous arithmetic rule with an opaque but equivalent resonance definition (for example, an indirect fixed lookup or encoded predicate) and avoid stating or hinting that valid links require different channels. No semantic edit can remove the bipartite core without changing the problem.
